# dsh-plugin-session-tags
Coloured tags for DeepSeek Harness sessions.

A tag is a **named** label, not a one-off colour: names and colours are defined
together in the sett

ings, the session title is tinted by its tag, and the tag's
name shows on the row's hover card — a s

tatus vocabulary that follows you across
devices, not a stray swatch on one row.

- **Sidebar row menu → 标签** opens a picker; the chosen tag tints that session's
sidebar title and sh

ows its label on the row's hover card.
- The same picker creates a tag on the spot: type a name, pic

k one of six colours
or any custom colour, then **新建并应用** tags the session immediately.
- **Settings

→ Plugins → 会话标签** renames tags, recolours them (palette or
custom), deletes them, or adds an empty

oute is unreachable the browser falls back to `localStorage`.
- Every window and device follows the

host's event stream, so a tag set on the
phone shows up on the desktop without a reload.

A tag colour is either a palette name (`green`, `amber`, `red`, `blue`, `purple`,
`gray` — theme tok
ens, so light/dark follow the app) or an explicit `#rrggbb`.
## Seats used
| Seat | Purpose |

| `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` | the `标签` row in a session's `...` menu |
| `shell.overlay

` | the picker dialog |
| `sidebar.session.row.hover` | the tag chip on the hover card |
| `settings
.plugins.tab` | tag definitions |

The title colour is a generated stylesheet rule keyed on the row's own
`data-row-key="session:<id>"`

attribute; unmounting the plugin removes it and the
shipped colours return.
## Host route
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The stream is what keeps windows and devices together: each accepted mutation is
written to every op

en stream. A page holds that stream only while it is visible —
hiding it closes the connection, show

ing it opens a new one, and the first frame
of a new stream is the current snapshot. So a sleeping p

hone or a hidden window
keeps nothing alive, and coming back is the catch-up. A client that cannot
e

stablish a stream at all pulls `/session-tags` on the next reconnect attempt, so
a stripped stream d
egrades to slow polling instead of a stale page.
